title: STREAM: Spatiotemporal Similarity-based Efficient Approximate Median with Tunable Granularity
problem: Exact median computation is expensive and fails to meet near real-time requirements; existing approximate methods ignore spatiotemporal data characteristics and lack application-specific accuracy-speed trade-offs.
motivation: Median is critical for measuring central tendency in data streams, but computational cost for large streaming datasets motivates approximate algorithms with tunable accuracy.
method: STREAM groups incoming data into buckets that exploit patterns in how data changes over time and space. Rather than recalculating each time, it reuses information from previous bucket states to speed up the median calculation. The algorithm includes a tunable-grained bucket mechanism—you can adjust the bucket size to control the trade-off between accuracy and speed, with finer buckets giving more precise results but taking longer. This allows applications to choose the speed-versus-accuracy balance that fits their needs.
key_novelty: STREAM is the first approximate median algorithm that takes advantage of patterns in how streaming data changes over time and space, while letting you adjust the bucket size to balance accuracy and speed.
contributions: Up to 47x speedup vs. DDSketch (10.1x average) with similar accuracy
Up to 71.2x speedup vs. KLL (10.1x average)

metrics.speedup: 47x vs. DDSketch, 71.2x vs. KLL (10.1x average for both)

limitations: Not discussed; applicability to non-streaming scenarios or discrete data types unclear.
